raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build` runs once per SWA KV cache group on every step, and on a decode step each build launches 8 small kernels before the decode graph can start. #60731 added `swa_decode_meta`, which builds the same metadata for a decode batch of up to 32 rows with one launch, but gated it to gfx942 together with the gfx942-only helpers. The kernel is plain Triton and writes the buffers that the gfx950 attention reads, so this PR also runs it with `--monokernel` on gfx950. The other helpers in `amd/ops` stay gfx942-only.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X, TP4, `--monokernel`, c=16: a decode step runs 49 fewer kernels before its first layer (42 instead of 91), and that section takes 0.220 ms instead of 0.416 ms.
- In a 12-point sweep against `main`, mean TPOT is 0.4% to 2.2% lower at every point with c ≤ 32 (8 of 8), and within ±0.5% at c ≥ 64, where decode batches exceed 32 rows and keep the current path.
- The metadata is identical to vLLM's ops. GSM8K and NIAH match `main` within run-to-run noise.
- Mixed and prefill steps, decode batches of more than 32 rows, and runs without `--monokernel` keep the current path.



## Validation



### End-to-end performance

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, FP8 KV, `--monokernel`, the same server arguments as in End-to-end accuracy (port 8005), with `sglang.bench_serve` on random data with `--random-range-ratio 0.8`. `main` (`8fae0ff58b`) and this PR (`main` plus this commit) on the same node, one sweep each.

| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------- | ------ | --------- | ------- | ----- | ------------- | ----------- | ----- | ---------- | -------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 170.37    | 132.68  | -22.1% | 4.90      | 4.79    | -2.2% | 4.93          | 4.82        | -2.2% | 772.10     | 795.31   | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 159.72    | 156.74  | -1.9%  | 5.95      | 5.85    | -1.7% | 5.98          | 5.88        | -1.7% | 1278.44    | 1300.53  | +1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 240.19    | 235.99  | -1.7%  | 7.97      | 7.88    | -1.1% | 8.07          | 8.00        | -0.9% | 1898.06    | 1920.57  | +1.2% |

| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 802.55    | 807.35  | +0.6%  | 18.35     | 18.36   | +0.1% | 18.78         | 18.80       | +0.1% | 3250.70    | 3248.98  | -0.1% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 1912.02   | 1914.32 | +0.1%  | 26.55     | 26.69   | +0.5% | 27.46         | 27.56       | +0.4% | 4339.35    | 4320.05  | -0.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 3713.22   | 3731.19 | +0.5%  | 39.64     | 39.63   | -0.0% | 41.19         | 41.18       | -0.0% | 5703.00    | 5701.82  | -0.0% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 942.06    | 981.04  | +4.1%  | 7.46      | 7.31    | -2.0% | 7.75          | 7.66        | -1.2% | 432.82     | 436.04   | +0.7% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 1804.32   | 1863.77 | +3.3%  | 20.33     | 20.17   | -0.8% | 21.20         | 21.00       | -0.9% | 668.39     | 670.18   | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 6260.73   | 6244.36 | -0.3%  | 67.48     | 67.63   | +0.2% | 73.66         | 73.18       | -0.7% | 801.48     | 800.41   | -0.1% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 1852.28   | 1899.30 | +2.5%  | 8.40      | 8.29    | -1.3% | 8.55          | 8.44        | -1.3% | 380.52     | 383.22   | +0.7% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 3779.92   | 3857.41 | +2.1%  | 24.80     | 24.70   | -0.4% | 26.03         | 26.00       | -0.1% | 545.50     | 545.92   | +0.1% |


TTFT and TPOT are means unless marked p50, in ms; throughput is output tokens/s. Sweep means: -0.79% TPOT, -0.76% p50 TPOT, +0.65% throughput. At c ≤ 32, TPOT is lower at all 8 points and throughput higher at all 8. At c ≥ 64 every mean TPOT and throughput delta is within ±0.5% (p50 TPOT within ±0.7%), as expected for the unchanged path. The change touches only decode steps, so the TTFT deltas are single-run noise: the -22.1% at 8192 / 1024 c=4 is the first point after server start, and the long-context TTFT rows go +2% to +4% while their TPOT goes down.

**Trace.** A profile of 20 pure decode steps at c=16 per arm: before the first layer, a step runs 91 kernels in 0.416 ms with vLLM's ops and 42 kernels in 0.220 ms with this PR. The 7 SWA builds of a step go from 7 launches each to 1.

### End-to-end accuracy

`main` (`8fae0ff58b`) and this PR (`main` plus this commit) on the same MI355X node, each run with a fresh server.


|                                                  | `main`                         | PR, run 1                      | PR, run 2                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, strict match                      | 0.9249 ± 0.0073 (1220 of 1319) | 0.9181 ± 0.0076 (1211 of 1319) | 0.9242 ± 0.0073 (1219 of 1319) |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, flexible extract                  | 0.9249 ± 0.0073                | 0.9174 ± 0.0076                | 0.9242 ± 0.0073                |
| NIAH `niah_single_2`, 32768 tokens (500 samples) | 0.972                          | 0.968                          | 0.978                          |
| NIAH `niah_single_2`, 65536 tokens (500 samples) | 0.942                          | 0.936                          | 0.942                          |


The two PR runs differ from each other by as much as from `main`: 8 of 1319 GSM8K questions and 5 of 500 NIAH samples at 32768 tokens, and `main` falls between them or ties them on every row. The metadata itself is bit-identical (see Correctness), so the spread comes from nondeterministic serving (batch composition under async scheduling).

### Correctness

`test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py::test_swa_decode_meta_matches_vllm_ops` runs vLLM's ops and the one-launch kernel on 300 random decode batches (causal and the DSpark draft block, block sizes 64 and 128, padded tokens, replay starts, null blocks) and requires every output to be equal. It passes on MI355X.

### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py   # 3 passed on MI355X
```

The SWA comparison test now also runs in `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`; it already ran on MI300.

## Details

**Changes.** `amd/ops/__init__.py` gains `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`, true with `--monokernel` on gfx942 or gfx950, and `swa_decode_meta.build` uses it instead of `enabled()`. `topk_pack`, the gfx942 top-k, the candidate logits, the Markov sampling and the draft LM head keep `enabled()`.

**Limitations.** Decode batches of more than 32 rows (for example c=64 without speculative decoding) keep the 8-launch build. Benchmarked only on MI355X at TP4.

### Existing PRs

I searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for the SWA metadata builder, `swa_decode_meta` and gfx950 decode metadata.

- [#58352](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58352) packs the ragged decode metadata straight into the graph buffers, removing the 2 copies of each build. On gfx950 with `--monokernel`, batches of up to 32 rows no longer reach that code after this PR; larger batches and runs without `--monokernel` still do.
- [#57756](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57756) changes the gfx950 sparse decode to consume dense top-k indices and fuses the metadata construction. It predates `swa_decode_meta`.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body: The performance section says it uses the server arguments from End-to-end accuracy, but that section lists none. Could you add the command, and say whether DSpark was on? The one-launch path takes at most 32 rows, so with DSpark at 6 draft tokens (7 rows per request) the target build uses it only up to c=4, and the c=8 to c=32 gains apply only without speculative decoding. Also, the Trace paragraph says each build goes from 7 launches to 1, but 91 - 42 = 49 = 7 x (8 - 1), which matches the 8 launches in the Overview.

inline_comments.body: The performance section says it uses the server arguments from End-to-end accuracy, but that section lists none. Could you add the command, and say whether DSpark was on? The one-launch path takes at most 32 rows, so with DSpark at 6 draft tokens (7 rows per request) the target build uses it only up to c=4, and the c=8 to c=32 gains apply only without speculative decoding. Also, the Trace paragraph says each build goes from 7 launches to 1, but 91 - 42 = 49 = 7 x (8 - 1), which matches the 8 launches in the Overview.
